content:
The image shows a mango leaf with white, powdery, dusty patches scattered across the surface. The patches are irregular and appear as a whitish-gray coating on the green leaf. There is no necrosis, no dark lesions, no die-back of tips, and no black sooty coating. The white powdery residue is the hallmark of fungal sporulation on the leaf surface.

This matches Powdery Mildew: superficial white powdery fungal growth on leaf surfaces, typically appearing as scattered white patches that can merge.
